controls.title: Evidence bundle verification
controls.claim: Receipts and evidence bundles verify, and a tampered, truncated or untrusted bundle fails verification. A check the bundle gives no input to is reported as not run and is never counted as passed. Evidence the bundle carries is validated whether or not anything requires it, and a recorded tape is replayed by the code `helm-ai-kernel replay` runs. Every check `verify` and `evidence inspect` run, except roots and evidence_pack_seal, reads the bundle only through an os.Root opened on its directory, and only from regular files: a path or symbolic link that leaves the bundle, an absolute symbolic link, a named pipe, a device or a socket is refused and never read, and the check that wanted the file fails (embedded_signature_trust skips it, and a directory walk passes over a link whose name it does not read). The layout check tests, lists and reads through the same os.Root. Directory opens require a directory handle and verify that it is the object checked before opening: a child directory swapped to a named pipe cannot block a listing or Open, and a different directory is refused. A file read whole is read up to 64 MiB; the EU AI Act scan reads at most 256 MiB and validates at most 1024 profiles per bundle, and a tape replay reads at most 256 MiB of entry files; the file a limit stops at fails the check by name.
protected_operations: `helm-ai-kernel verify` over an EvidencePack bundle.
`helm-ai-kernel evidence inspect` over an EvidencePack bundle; it reaches its verdict through the same code as `verify`.
bypass_assumptions: A self-attested seal is rejected by default; a caller that opts into accepting one gets weaker evidence.
Chain tamper detection is layered (the recomputed receipt hash, the raw-bytes hash and prev_hash linkage), so no single deletion removes it; the removal proof covers the manifest file-hash check.

A bundle that omits optional evidence (a receipt chain, manifest file hashes, connector evidence, an EU AI Act profile, host evidence, a replay gate, signed receipts) still verifies: those checks are NOT_RUN, and VERIFIED covers only the checks that ran. A caller that needs one of them must name it with `--require-check`.
The field-presence checks (policy_decision_hashes, connector_evidence, eu_ai_act_profile, replay_determinism) recompute nothing; their details say so.

Replay material is validated without gate G2: a determinism manifest with diverging hashes fails, and a tape that carries entries is replayed and fails if it does not replay. Under G2 a tape with no entries fails, as `replay` reports NOT_RUN for it. The entry files of a tape are sized before any is read, and entry files past 256 MiB in all fail by the name of the file that passes the bound, with none read. The files in 05_DIFFS are read as replay differences only under G2, where an empty file whose name starts with a dot is a placeholder. A tape that replays, in a bundle without a determinism manifest, states no replay result and leaves replay_determinism NOT_RUN. Replaying serves recorded inputs back; the run is not re-executed.

roots and evidence_pack_seal read the bundle by path through core/pkg/evidence. It refuses a symbolic link anywhere on the path of 00_INDEX.json, of the seal file and of every indexed file, and a last component that is not a regular file, by looking (os.Lstat) before it opens the file; a file swapped in between those two steps is not caught there.

The layout check `verify` and `evidence inspect` add for a bundle in the canonical layout (core/pkg/conform) tests whether the mandatory files and directories exist, lists the bundle directory and 99_EXT, and reads 00_INDEX.json through os.Root; a mandatory name or 99_EXT that is a symbolic link out of the bundle is an issue and is never listed. Whether the bundle is in the canonical layout and whether it carries a conformance signature are tested with os.Stat by path, which follows symbolic links and opens nothing.
Each check opens the bundle directory by path when it starts. A bundle directory replaced while it is being verified is outside this control.

A symbolic link that stays inside the bundle is followed. A path 00_INDEX.json or manifest.json names must match the directory listing letter for letter, so a case-insensitive file system fails it as a case-sensitive one does.

The EU AI Act scan matches the member name in any letter case, as encoding/json does. A .json file that does not parse fails eu_ai_act_profile only when it names the profile, in any letter case, as plain text or as a member the scan still finds; otherwise it is counted as unparsed in the reason. A failed eu_ai_act_profile reason lists the first 10 issues and counts the rest. The launch id and evidence graph `evidence inspect` prints are left out when their files are refused.

Reads that skip instead of failing: embedded_signature_trust skips a receipt or attestation file or directory it cannot read, and reads no receipts when the receipts directory is refused (chain_integrity, lamport_monotonicity and policy_decision_hashes fail that bundle); host_evidence skips a host evidence directory, or a directory under one, that it cannot list. The walks of eu_ai_act_profile, host_evidence and embedded_signature_trust do not follow a symbolic link: one whose name ends in a suffix the check reads is opened through os.Root, and any other, including a link to a directory inside or outside the bundle, is passed over without being named.

Under the host evidence directories a file named like a correlation or verification report that parses as one is not verified as a receipt chain; one that holds receipts is, and one that does not parse fails.
`helm-ai-kernel replay` is outside this control: it replays the tape with the code replay_determinism runs and does not check the bundle seal.

controls.title: Mandates only narrow on delegation
controls.claim: When helm-gateway's authority adapter applies a helm.authority.provision.v1 or narrow.v1 plan, the authority store's transaction (authorityrows.Tx) delegates a mandate only within every mandate above it as they stand at that moment, in each term the rule compares (effect types, per-call limit, approval threshold, validity window, targets, risk classes, approval requirements); only the parent's holder delegates, over a chain with no revoked link, and no stop on the tenant, the delegator or a mandate of the chain may be active. A mandate narrows in place only to terms within its own and never replaces a condition it has. A new limit on a delegated mandate is no higher than the lowest limit of its unit, measure, window and span on any mandate above it, and a limit is lowered, never raised. A narrowing bumps, in the same transaction, the version of the row it changes (a revoked or narrowed mandate, a lowered limit) or, when it adds a limit, of the limit's scope (the mandate, or the tenant). A root mandate needs an active human approver who is neither the requester nor its holder (HELM-750, ADR-0001). Admission re-checks every link of the chain it resolves against the link above it. The store's own Stop and Lift are not part of this claim.
protected_operations: Delegating a mandate, narrowing it in place, revoking it, and adding or lowering a limit on it, in the authority rows.
Activating a root mandate.
Applying a helm.authority.provision.v1 or narrow.v1 plan through helm-gateway's authority adapter, and the admission of an effect under the chain those rows form.
bypass_assumptions: The schema holds no narrowing constraint. A role with INSERT or UPDATE on authority_mandates or authority_limits can write a row wider than the one above it without the store. Admission re-checks every link of the chain it resolves and denies a wider mandate (DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION, bypass test below). A limit written that way is not compared with the one above it again; admission counts every limit of every mandate of the chain and the tenant's, so the lower limit above it still binds.

Only a plan applied by the authority adapter, and EnsurePrincipals, write the rows in a shipped binary; admission enforces what they say (CTL-052), not how they were written. The Store methods that wrap the same Tx calls in their own transaction (Store.CreateMandate, Delegate, Narrow, Revoke, CreateLimit, LowerLimit) have no shipped caller; the Postgres-gated tests drive the Tx code through them, and the plan path is what is enforced.

A plan's root mandate takes its requester and approver from the gateway's approval record of the plan attempt (CTL-053). The store checks that the approver is an active human distinct from the requester and the holder, and takes the pair as given: the WideningApproval argument stays a bare pair of principal ids for any other caller of the library.
Narrowing a mandate in place leaves the mandates delegated from it as they are. Admission holds them to the narrowed terms; a new delegation from them is refused by the store.

Conditions are not compared when delegating: admission requires every link's condition to hold, so a child's condition only narrows. A narrowing in place keeps or adds a condition and never replaces one.

Store.Stop and Store.Lift have no shipped caller, and are not claimed: the gateway's own stops and lifts are admission.Service.Stop and Lift (CTL-055). Delegate reads the same table (authority_stops) and the same scope_kind:scope_key key that the gateway's stop writer, admission.Service.Stop, writes. The tests that show an active stop refusing a delegation write that stop with Store.Stop, not with the gateway's writer.

Tx.CreateLimit reads the chain without locking its mandate rows and FOR SHARE-locks only the ancestor limit rows that already exist. A concurrent CreateLimit or SetLimit that adds a limit to an ancestor can commit alongside it, so a mandate's new limit can stand above an ancestor limit of the same unit, measure, window and span. This stays authority-neutral only because admission counts every limit of every mandate of the chain, so the lower limit binds; no test drives that race.
That a plan applied by helm-gateway's authority adapter goes through authorityrows.Tx (core/pkg/gateway/adapters/provision/apply.go) is established by code reachability, not by a removal proof.

The removal proofs run on a scripted driver, without a database. They show that each check is in the code path and that the statement bumping a control row's version is issued by the transaction. What Postgres then does with it (the row lock, the bump itself, waiting for a concurrent narrowing, constraints, tenant isolation) is proved by the Postgres-gated tests, which are listed in scripts/ci/postgres-proofs.txt and carry no removal proof.

controls.title: Effect gateway admission
controls.claim: helm-gateway admits an effect only in one READ COMMITTED Postgres transaction bound to the token's tenant (ADR-0001): idempotency first on (tenant, key) with a request digest; the mandate resolved from the token's principal and the effect type; the tenant row, the chain's principals, the mandates root to leaf, the effect type and the limits locked FOR SHARE; stops read after the locks; counters locked FOR UPDATE; then a pure decide. HELM_CP_IDENTITY_JWKS_URL, HELM_CP_IDENTITY_ISSUER, HELM_CP_IDENTITY_AUDIENCE (helm-gateway:<env>), HELM_CP_IDENTITY_ACTOR, HELM_CP_IDENTITY_MAX_TTL, HELM_CP_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_CNF and HELM_CP_IDENTITY_OUTBOUND_CA_BUNDLE_FILE; serve refuses to start without the first four.

Authority rows (tenants, principals, effect types, mandates, limits, stops) are written by core/pkg/kernel/authority/authorityrows, which the gateway's authority adapter and EnsurePrincipals call (CTL-046); the gateway trusts the rows it finds.

helm-gateway ships in the kernel container image, and the chart deploys it only when gateway.enabled is set (off by default); where no gateway runs, nothing here is enforced.

ListAttempts is not a change feed: updated_at is the start time of the transaction that wrote the row, so a row written by a long transaction can commit behind an updated_at a client already holds. A client that syncs with updated_after re-reads a window before its cursor.

controls.title: Gateway approval decisions
controls.claim: helm-gateway records at most one decision per ESCALATED attempt, by an active human principal of the tenant distinct from the requester (ADR-0001 I6), with a helm.gateway.decide token bound by RFC 9396 authorization_details to that attempt and action and used once: its jti is recorded in Postgres in the decision's transaction. The approval digest must equal the attempt's, the escalation must not have expired, and an approval of a high, irreversible or authority-widening effect, judged on the risk re-admission computes, needs a step-up proof: a compact helm.gateway.stepup token of the decide token's approver and tenant, verified like any gateway token, fresh (an iat, and an exp at most 300 seconds after it) and bound by authorization_details (helm_step_up) to the attempt, the approval digest and the method webauthn, stating user_verified true. Its jti is used once, recorded in Postgres in the approval's transaction after the decide token's, and the approval record keeps the proof exactly as received with its issuer, jti and method. Without a valid, unused proof the approval fails closed (STEP_UP_REQUIRED), the attempt stays ESCALATED and neither token is used up; a proof for an effect that needs none is ignored. A token past exp plus the skew by the database clock is refused, so a purge never makes one replayable. Approve re-runs admission in the same transaction, re-reading stops, the mandate chain and counters, so the attempt becomes ADMITTED or DENIED; a refused precondition leaves it ESCALATED. Cancel follows ESCALATED or ADMITTED to CANCELLED only, voiding the permit and releasing held exposure in the same transaction, for the requester's propose token or an active human operator's single-use stop token bound by authorization_details (helm_effect_cancel) to that attempt.
config: The HELM_CP_IDENTITY_* token configuration of CTL-052; decide and stop tokens are minted per decision by the Control Plane and carry iss, jti and exp. A step-up proof is one more such token (one audience, the issuer's keys, the configured actor, the certificate binding when required) and needs no configuration of its own.
protected_operations: Approve, Reject and Cancel of helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService on helm-gateway serve.
bypass_assumptions: A step-up proof is the issuer's attestation that it verified the approver's WebAuthn assertion over the approval digest, not the gateway's own check: the gateway holds no credential registry, so a compromised Control Plane issuer can mint a proof as it can mint a decide token (the trust limits of CTL-052 apply).
A medium effect a mandate escalates (approval_required) is approved without step-up, and a proof presented for it is ignored: it cannot refuse the approval, and it is not used up or recorded.
An escalation past its expiry is refused; the River job of CTL-056 moves it to EXPIRED.
A decide token binds the attempt and action; the approver sees and hashes the arguments through GetAttemptContent, which this slice serves but cannot force a client to use.
Releasing an ADMITTED attempt keeps its distinct-value rows, so the value still counts as seen in its bucket.
The trust limits of CTL-052 (ADR-0005 issuer trust, no deployment yet) apply.

controls.title: Gateway dispatch claim and observation
controls.claim: helm-gateway dispatches and observes an attempt only for the active workload principal (agent or service) it was proposed through, its requester actor or its requester principal, in the token's tenant and workspace with a helm.gateway.execute token, and dispatches it only through one claim transaction, which records the dispatcher, committed before any provider I/O (ADR-0001 §1, TA §4.1): it locks the attempt and its unused permit, re-locks the authority rows FOR SHARE and reads the stops after them. An active stop (EMERGENCY_STOP_FENCED), an expired permit (PERMIT_EXPIRED), any change to a row the permit was issued under (AUTHORITY_CHANGED) or a mandate outside its validity (MANDATE_OUTSIDE_VALIDITY) voids the permit, releases the held exposure and records CANCELLED; otherwise the permit is consumed once and the attempt becomes DISPATCHING with a fence. The adapter's SENT becomes DISPATCHED and is read back; NOT_SENT becomes OBSERVED(FAILED) with the adapter's reason and releases the hold; INDEFINITE becomes UNKNOWN and keeps it. A repeated Dispatch returns the stored attempt, and UNKNOWN or a DISPATCHING attempt past its fence is only ever read back by Observe, never sent again. A FAILED read-back that rests only on the object's absence is inconclusive until the fence has passed. Observe records the typed result the effect type defines, with evidence_digest and result_ref, SHA-256 over the result's JCS form, and in the same transaction consumes the held exposure (SUCCEEDED, or an object that contradicts the effect) or releases it (absent after the fence) (HELM-751 s3). Adapter invocation context carries the authenticated tenant/workspace, requester, original attempt/permit/claim, expiry and admitted resource quote from the locked rows, never from arguments. Observe reconstructs the same context without granting another dispatch.
config: HELM_GATEWAY_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT (default 2m) bounds one adapter call; the fence is the claim time plus it plus a one-minute grace.
The HELM_CP_IDENTITY_* token configuration of CTL-052; execute tokens are minted for workload principals only.
protected_operations: Dispatch and Observe of helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService on helm-gateway serve.
bypass_assumptions: A provider that applies a write more than a minute after the gateway stopped waiting can be read back as FAILED before it lands; the fence bounds this, it does not remove it.
UNKNOWN is reconciled by the reconcile job (CTL-056) or a workload's Observe.
Stops are written by the Stop RPC (CTL-055) or core/pkg/kernel/authority/authorityrows (CTL-046).
An observation is what the adapter read back from the provider (trust class provider_readback); the gateway checks its shape, not its truth.
A count-unit effect's exposure settles at its observed outcome; the SETTLED state is left to model-call settlement (HELM-752).
The trust limits of CTL-052 (ADR-0005 issuer trust) apply.

controls.title: Gateway stops and lifts
controls.claim: helm-gateway's Stop writes a stop row and bumps its scope's control row (tenant, principal, mandate or effect type) in one transaction, for an active human operator of the tenant with a single-use helm.gateway.stop token, idempotent on (tenant, key) with a request digest (HELM-751 s3b). The stop token names the stop request (authorization_details helm_stop), and concurrent Stops under one key make one stop. Admissions after it are DENIED and admitted attempts are CANCELLED at their dispatch claim, both EMERGENCY_STOP_FENCED; a principal stop covers the requester, the workload that carries its call (act.sub), the dispatcher and its act, and a stopped approver cannot approve. A call already dispatched is not retracted and is read back as usual. Lift, the only way to create a helm.authority.lift attempt, proposes one for the stop its single-use stop token names (helm_stop_lift); the lift is blocked by every stop but that one. Every helm.authority.* effect escalates whatever its risk row or approval_required says, counts against no limit, needs a distinct human approver and fails closed without step-up (STEP_UP_REQUIRED).
config: The HELM_CP_IDENTITY_* token configuration of CTL-052; stop tokens are minted per operator action and carry iss, jti and exp.
protected_operations: Stop and Lift of helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService on helm-gateway serve, and the Console's emergency stop (HELM-799) through Stop.
bypass_assumptions: Step-up does not exist yet, so no lift can be approved: a stop through the gateway stays until it expires, or until the authority-row store (CTL-046) lifts it with a distinct approver.
A lift attempt that were ADMITTED has no applier yet: applying the lift at dispatch lands with step-up.
An operator is whoever the gateway's principal rows record as an active human; the token's issuer is trusted as in CTL-052.

controls.title: Gateway escalation timers and reconciliation jobs
controls.claim: helm-gateway enqueues River jobs in its own Postgres in the transaction that makes them due (TA §6.2): an escalation's expiry job with the escalation, and a reconciliation job with the dispatch claim. The expiry job writes EXPIRED (APPROVAL_TIMEOUT) under the attempt's row lock, so an approval and the expiry make exactly one transition. The reconciliation job reads the attempt back with doubling backoff, waits out a dispatch fence without spending an attempt, never dispatches, and at the last attempt moves an attempt still unresolved to ESCALATED_TO_HUMAN with its reservation held, in a transaction of its own, whatever made the read-back fail. A graceful stop lets running jobs finish (a 15 s soft stop) (HELM-751 s3b).
config: helm-gateway migrate applies River's migrations with the gateway schema; /readyz requires both current. River's tables need the helm_gateway grants listed in the chart's 002_grants.sql.
Defaults: the first read-back 30s after the claim, backoff 30s doubling to 30m, 12 read-backs (about four hours).
protected_operations: Escalation expiry and UNKNOWN reconciliation for every attempt helm-gateway serve admits or dispatches.
bypass_assumptions: Jobs run in helm-gateway serve; with no serve process running, nothing expires or reconciles until one starts. Jobs are durable rows and run late, never not at all.
A last attempt whose hand-off transaction itself fails (the database unreachable) is discarded by River; the attempt stays UNKNOWN with its hold, and Observe still resolves it.
River's tables have no row security; job arguments carry tenant, workspace and attempt IDs only (follow-up L3). All jobs share one worker pool (follow-up L4).
River's tables carry job arguments (tenant, workspace and attempt IDs) outside row security; every job binds its own transaction to the tenant it names.

controls.title: Gateway worker endpoint and episode isolation
controls.claim: helm-gateway serves its effect types to episode workers as MCP tools at /mcp on the worker listener (HELM-751 K3), stateless, in the 2026-07-28 revision and the legacy initialize handshake. Tenant, workspace, principal, actor and episode come only from the verified worker token; only agent principals are served; tools/list names the effect types of the caller's live mandate chains that the gateway performs; and a tool call is proposed, admitted, dispatched and observed under the same admission transaction and permit as any effect, the permit claimed by the worker's own principal and never under a helm.gateway.execute token. An escalation is a structured non-error result, a denial a tool error with its reason code, and the same request replayed is the same attempt. An attempt proposed under an episode token records the claim's episode and takes its work item as its case; a token with an episode claim proposes under that work item only and reads only the attempts of its own episode that its own principal proposed, in every read of an attempt (HELM-751 N1). Public executors use a separate listener and audience, a signed canonical client marker, complete episode linkage and a strict 900-second maximum lease. Internal worker tokens, including short ones, cannot authenticate there. Registered custom argument schemas are compiled as closed objects at startup and enforced against the complete input before any admission transaction. Exact published builtin schemas retain their native semantic validators; a changed declaration cannot inherit that exemption.
config: --executor-listen, HELM_GATEWAY_EXECUTOR_AUDIENCE=helm-gateway-executor:<env> and HELM_GATEWAY_EXECUTOR_MAX_TTL<=15m: public executor profile, with required CP actor, signed helm_executor client, complete helm_episode, no cnf and strict expiry.

--worker-listen, HELM_GATEWAY_WORKER_AUDIENCE and HELM_GATEWAY_WORKER_MAX_TTL: the worker listener, which serves /mcp and the model endpoints to episode tokens only. It needs HELM_GATEWAY_MODEL_ROUTES_FILE.
Nothing of its own: the tools are the effect types that the gateway's adapters declare as grantable with an argument schema, and serve refuses to start when one cannot be given a tool name.
protected_operations: tools/list and tools/call of the MCP endpoint on the worker listener of helm-gateway serve, and GetAttempt, GetAttemptContent, ListAttempts and the stored response of a model call for a token that carries an episode claim.
bypass_assumptions: Token trust is ADR-0005's: a compromised Control Plane issuer can mint an episode token for any seat and episode. The episode is the token's claim, not something the gateway verifies independently.
Who can reach the worker listener is the deployment's network policy, not this code: the listener has no client certificate, so a token is all it asks for.
An attempt proposed without an episode token, such as the Control Plane's own, records no episode, and the isolation binds only a token that carries one.
A worker can make any call its mandates admit: the endpoint limits what a call may name, not what a model chooses to ask for within its authority.

A composition declares its closed, versioned JSON result schema at startup. An Artifact result is accepted only when its canonical bytes, content digest and declared schema agree; the schema does not upgrade the provider trust class. Results are limited to 1 MiB and oversized snapshots must fail explicitly.

tools/call runs the dispatch in the request: a client that hangs up does not stop it, and a call that outlives CallTimeout is answered as a failure to repeat, with the attempt left for a read-back or the reconciliation job.

controls.title: Kernel bounded retained work reassignment
controls.claim: A distinct-human-approved and stepped-up Kernel authority effect installs one current work reassignment generation after a locked, complete native attempt scan. A signed worker or executor successor claim resolves its exact grant and member in the tenant ledger on every retained status or replay read. The replay returns only the original result and cannot dispatch, observe, approve, copy a permit or move an exposure. The old episode is fenced for both new proposals and idempotent replay. A revoked, expired, stopped or superseded grant fails closed. An empty native drain has no retained members. This is the Kernel boundary; Control Plane preparation, assignment and issuance remain separate obligations.
config: HELM_GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL and gateway schema migration 12 for tenant-isolated current generation and member rows.
Worker and executor listener JWKS issuer, audience, actor and profile configuration; the signed helm_reassignment claim carries a reference, never member authority.
protected_operations: The exact retained status/result of listed work attempts at MCP tools/call, helm_attempt_get and GetAttempt; original effect dispatch and authority stay on the original attempt.
bypass_assumptions: The Control Plane issuer is trusted for recipient assignment and the application digest; Kernel checks its own grant and native attempt ledger, not the Control Plane database.
A valid grant is not evidence of the Control Plane's durable application, hosted issuance closure or live managed-client acceptance.
GetAttemptContent and ListAttempts retain ordinary episode isolation; the grant does not authorize raw historical content.

controls.title: Gateway signed decision and outcome receipts
controls.claim: Every decision helm-gateway admission writes through recordDecision commits in its own transaction with one signed receipt (helm-tracker#276); tested for ADMITTED, DENIED, ESCALATED, the stepped-up re-admission of an approved escalation, a stop's lift and a model-call admission. The receipt is a classical Ed25519 receipt.v5 envelope over the attempt row the decision's UPDATE returned: decision_id is <attempt_id>:<version>, args_hash the hex SHA-256 of the exact argument bytes the attempt stored (its argument_digest, not a JCS re-encoding), policy_hash the SHA-256 of the locked authority versions, and output_hash the SHA-256 of a closed helm.gateway.receipt-binding.v1 document, stored as exact JCS bytes with it, which also binds the approver's workload and any step-up proof used up. The outcome of every admitted effect is receipted the same way, in the transaction that records it (recordOutcome): OBSERVED and RECONCILED, SUCCEEDED or FAILED, from a read-back of Dispatch, Observe, the reconciliation job or the MCP tools, from an adapter's NOT_SENT answer, and from a model call's confirmed, estimated, refused or late-confirmed settlement, and a model call's SETTLED; tested for each. An outcome receipt's status is the outcome state and its verdict empty; its policy_hash is that of the authority versions the permit was issued under (the decision receipt's), and its output_hash is the SHA-256 of its own closed document, helm.gateway.outcome-binding.v1, so decision receipts keep receipt-binding.v1 byte for byte. That document binds the attempt core (tenant, workspace, attempt, version, from and to state, effect type, request, target and argument digests, permit, authority versions), the outcome and its basis, the stored observation it rests on, what established it (read-back, NOT_SENT or model call), whether a read-back found the object absent, what it did to the reservation, every exposure as the ledger holds it after the write, and for a model call its money row (currency, held, estimated, confirmed and billable micros) and the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 form of its stored usage, so a late usage report re-settles with a receipt of the new amounts. The builder refuses a (from, to) pair no outcome write makes, an observation of another outcome, and settlement facts that do not fit how the outcome was established. Receipts form one hash chain per (tenant, workspace): the chain row is the last row lock the transaction takes on a pre-existing row, so a workspace's decisions and outcomes serialize on it until commit; lamport_clock is the sequence, prev_hash the predecessor's chain hash, and the ledger refuses a fork, a second genesis or a reused sequence. A signing failure, a refused profile, a missing observation or a moved head rolls the decision or the outcome back (an attempt whose outcome rolled back keeps its state for a later read-back), and deferred constraint triggers (migrations 15 and 16) refuse at commit any attempt that enters ADMITTED, DENIED or ESCALATED, or enters (or is rewritten at a new version in) OBSERVED, RECONCILED or SETTLED, without the receipt of that version and state, whoever writes it, including an older gateway still serving during an upgrade. Migration 16 locks authority_effect_attempts before it alters authority_receipts, and pins both fence functions' search_path to the gateway schema, so a look-alike authority_receipts on a writer's search_path or in its temporary schema satisfies neither fence. admission refuses a nil signer and one whose receipts are not classical Ed25519 that verify offline under its published key; serve refuses to start without HELM_GATEWAY_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY_FILE (a 32-byte seed, never a passphrase or all zeros) and a key id, verbatim or derived from a prefix and the key's fingerprint. The runtime role may only SELECT and INSERT receipt rows, and the stored chain verifies with receiptverify under the gateway key alone. EffectAttempt.receipts names each receipt by chain, sequence, chain hash and key id.
config: HELM_GATEWAY_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY_FILE (a 32-byte Ed25519 seed, hex or base64) and HELM_GATEWAY_RECEIPT_KEY_ID or HELM_GATEWAY_RECEIPT_KEY_ID_PREFIX; the chart mounts gateway.receipts.existingSecret, or its autoSeed Secret, into the gateway Pod only, and by default sets the prefix.

Gateway schema migration 15: authority_receipt_chains and authority_receipts under forced row security, and the deferred decision-receipt fence on authority_effect_attempts. The chart's 002_grants.sql gives the runtime role SELECT, INSERT only on authority_receipts.
Gateway schema migration 16: authority_receipts also holds OBSERVED, RECONCILED and SETTLED receipts, and the deferred outcome-receipt fence on authority_effect_attempts.
protected_operations: Every ADMITTED, DENIED and ESCALATED write of helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService Propose, Approve and Lift, the MCP tools on the worker and executor listeners, and the model gateway's admissions on helm-gateway serve.

Every OBSERVED, RECONCILED and SETTLED write of helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService Dispatch and Observe, the reconcile job, the MCP tools' dispatch and read-back, and the model gateway's settlement on helm-gateway serve.
bypass_assumptions: The receipt format is receipt.v5, an interim: the gateway's own facts are signed only through output_hash, and the binding bytes are retained beside the receipt. The gateway is one of the producers Mindburn-Labs/helm-tracker#53 moves to the DSSE v6 envelope; receipt.v5 stays verify-only after that. A gateway receipt's args_hash is the exact-argument-bytes digest, not the JCS-arguments hash contracts.Receipt documents for other producers.

Receipts cover decisions and outcomes. Not receipted, and not fenced: ESCALATED to REJECTED and EXPIRED (no effect was admitted), CANCELLED (a refused claim or a cancellation: nothing was dispatched, and the decision receipt stays the attempt's last), the lifecycle in between (DISPATCHING, DISPATCHED, UNKNOWN), and ESCALATED_TO_HUMAN (no outcome is known, and an outcome a human later establishes has no gateway write path today). An effect API attempt's reservation stays held there, but a cut model call (UNKNOWN) has already moved its hold to estimated, spending budget as an estimate; that spend is receipted only when a provider confirmation reconciles the call (RECONCILED, then SETTLED), and never if none arrives. There are no start or heartbeat lifecycle receipts; delivery gate 2 needs the decision and the outcome only. COMPENSATED is in the schema but nothing writes it.

The outcome fence checks that a receipt exists for the row's (tenant, attempt, version, state) when the state or the version changes. The runtime role holds UPDATE on authority_effect_attempts, so it can rewrite the outcome, its basis or its reason in place at the same version without the fence noticing; the signed receipt still records what was settled, and a reader compares the row with it.

An outcome receipt binds the one observation its outcome rests on. Distinct provider facts a later read-back records after the attempt settled are kept as observations, not receipted; a model call's late usage is receipted because it re-settles the attempt at a new version.

During an upgrade to schema 16, an older gateway's outcome fails at commit: an effect API attempt stays DISPATCHING, DISPATCHED or UNKNOWN for the reconciliation job the claim enqueued, and a model call's settlement is not written, so the attempt keeps its hold and is reconciled as the model gateway documents for any settlement that cannot be written. Outcomes an older gateway committed before the migration keep no receipt.

The signing key lives in the gateway process and its Secret. Whoever holds the seed, or the gateway's runtime database role together with it, can sign and insert a receipt the chain accepts; a row inserted without the key does not verify offline.

A missing receipt is detected only as a gap before a later receipt. The runtime role moves the chain head on every append; the database owner can also delete the newest receipts and rewind the head, which the chain alone cannot reveal. Chain export and external anchoring are the follow-up.

With gateway.receipts.autoSeed the key is generated by the chart and kept through Helm lookup. A pipeline that renders with helm template, or a deleted Secret, starts a new key (and, with the default derived key id, a new key id); receipts signed before verify only under the old public key, which must be recorded (helm-gateway receipt-key) to stay verifiable.

The receipt.v5 timestamp is outside the signed preimage; the next receipt's prev_hash covers it, and decided_at (a decision) or settled_at (an outcome) is signed through the binding. Order is the signed sequence.
The ledger fence is a database trigger; the database owner (or a superuser in replica mode) can drop or bypass it.

Outcome receipts sign helm.gateway.outcome-binding.v1, a second closed document beside receipt-binding.v1. receiptverify checks their signature, chain links and output_hash like any receipt.v5; reading what an outcome binding says needs its schema, which the verifier lane adds.

An outcome binding's settlement facts are the exposure and model-call rows its own transaction read just before signing. The runtime role holds UPDATE on authority_exposures and authority_model_calls, so a later in-place rewrite is not fenced; the signed receipt keeps what was settled, and a reader compares the rows with it.

Migration 16 takes authority_effect_attempts before authority_receipts, so an older gateway's decision cannot deadlock it. A transaction that reads authority_receipts and then writes an attempt (Propose's work-effect replay check) can still form a cycle with it; PostgreSQL's deadlock detector aborts one side, and a failed migration records nothing and runs again.

The fences' search_path is pinned to the schema that holds authority_receipts when migration 16 runs (read from pg_class); a deployment that moved the tables to another schema afterwards would have to pin the functions again.

A model call's settlement clears expired replay bodies tenant-wide and keeps those rows locked until it commits, through the signing of its receipts; concurrent settlements skip rows another is clearing (SKIP LOCKED) rather than wait for them.

controls.title: Gateway receipts verify offline with their bindings
controls.claim: A reader verifies helm-gateway's signed decision and outcome receipts (CTL-059) offline, the gateway's own facts included (helm-tracker#276). receiptverify, receipt_verify and the WASM verifier take a gateway receipt's binding document (bundle member gateway_bindings, receipt id to the base64 of the exact bytes, or receipt_verify --binding <receipt_id>=<file>) and run a binding check: it passes only when every supplied binding's receipt is signed under receipt.v5, the binding's SHA-256 is that receipt's signed output_hash, the binding is the closed document its binding_version names (helm.gateway.receipt-binding.v1 for a decision, helm.gateway.outcome-binding.v1 for an outcome; an unknown version fails) in its own JCS form, and its chain id (length-framed from its tenant and workspace), sequence, attempt and version, state, reason code, policy hash and argument digest equal the receipt's session_id, lamport_clock, decision_id, effect_id, status, reason_code, policy_hash and args_hash; a decision binding's verdict and decided_at equal the receipt's verdict and timestamp, and an outcome binding's state is OBSERVED, RECONCILED or SETTLED, it names its permit, the receipt's verdict is empty and its settled_at equals the receipt's timestamp (outside the receipt.v5 preimage, bound by these rows). A binding for a receipt the bundle does not hold, or for a receipt id the bundle holds twice, fails; with no binding the check is not_applicable, never a pass. The result counts gateway_receipts and bindings_checked, and receipt_verify --require-bindings (Options.RequireGatewayBindings) fails a gateway receipt that has no binding, so exit 0 then covers every gateway receipt's own facts. helm-gateway serves GET /api/v1/receipt-keyring on its API listener, public and read-only, in the Kernel's keyring shape (CTL-050) under its own label, gateway-receipt-keyring.v1, for the key it signs receipts with, and refuses to start with a signer it cannot publish. GetAttemptReceipts returns an attempt's receipts as the exact stored envelope and binding bytes, to a helm.gateway.read token that can read the attempt (its tenant, workspace and episode scope). ExportReceiptChain returns receipts from_seq to to_seq, at most 256, of the chain of the token's tenant and workspace, in order, as the document receipt_verify checks offline; it refuses a workspace_id other than the token's and an episode token, reads a range that runs past the chain's head up to the head and names it (one that starts past it is not found), and never returns a range with a gap. A frozen gateway chain of three decisions and one outcome keeps verifying.
config: None beyond CTL-059's receipt key: the keyring describes HELM_GATEWAY_RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY_FILE's public half under its key id. One export holds at most admission.MaxExportReceipts (256) receipts; the keyring route allows the Kernel's public route class rate (120 a second, bursts of 240) per gateway process.
protected_operations: helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService GetAttemptReceipts and ExportReceiptChain, and GET /api/v1/receipt-keyring, on helm-gateway serve's API listener.
receipt_verify --receipt with gateway_bindings or --binding, with or without --require-bindings, and receiptverify.VerifyJSON in the WASM verifier.
bypass_assumptions: The binding check proves the key holder signed these gateway facts. It cannot show the facts are true of a ledger the verifier does not see, and it says nothing of a receipt whose binding is not supplied: without --require-bindings exit 0 does not cover such a receipt. The WASM bridge has no require option; its caller compares bindings_checked with gateway_receipts.

Trust in the key is the reader's: the keyring is public and unauthenticated by design. Over plain HTTP it can be substituted in transit; fetch it over the gateway's TLS listener or pin the key out of band (helm-gateway receipt-key). Behind HELM_TLS_CLIENT_AUTH=require the API listener also asks the reader for a client certificate.

An export proves its range is contiguous and signed. It does not show that nothing follows to_seq: the database owner can delete the newest receipts and rewind the head (CTL-059); head_seq is what the ledger said when it was read.

Continuation and reassignment grants do not extend to receipts: such a token reads the receipts of the attempts its own scope covers only. An episode token cannot export the chain, which holds every episode's decisions in its workspace.
The keyring route's rate bound is per process, shared by all callers, as the Kernel's public class is; a caller exhausting it delays other readers of the public key, never a decision.

Only the binding versions the verifier names are recognised; a receipt that commits to another fails the binding check until the verifier learns that version. A gateway receipt is recognised by its session_id prefix (helm-gateway:), which its producer writes.

controls.title: TON Acton runs local, fork and testnet only, and never tenant code beside a key
controls.claim: helm-gateway performs TON Acton operations as gateway effects (helm-tracker#266) in the owner's scope. Local operations: project new and init, version, doctor, env, doc, build, check, format, format_check, test, wrapper generation, compile, disasm, library info and fetch. Forks of testnet and mainnet state: script.fork_testnet and script.fork_mainnet. Testnet operations: library.publish_testnet, library.topup_testnet and source.verify_testnet. Two classes are refused at Propose, before any mandate, adapter or database read, and have no adapter: every mainnet operation (library.publish_mainnet, library.topup_mainnet, script.mainnet, source.verify_mainnet) with ERR_TON_MAINNET_REFUSED, and script.testnet with ERR_TON_TENANT_CODE_WITH_KEY_REFUSED, because an Acton script is tenant-authored code that can read the process environment and files and must not share a process with a signing key. Acton can execute tenant files in every operation except version, doctor, env, doc, project new and project init, so those operations are declared only when the operator configures an isolation command (HELM_GATEWAY_TON_ACTON_ISOLATION_CMD, a JSON array: the program and arguments that run Acton under another uid or in a container with no access to the gateway's credential files); without it they fail closed at declaration. The adapter re-validates every argument itself (no flag-shaped or escaping path, no network other than testnet, only the properties the operation takes), refuses a workspace that holds a .env or wallets.toml in the project or any directory above it up to the tenant root (Acton loads them on its own), and compares a declared acton_version or tolk_compiler_version with what the configured binary reports for acton --version, refusing on any mismatch or any pin the binary does not report. The testnet wallet secret is held by the gateway's custody (one owner-only file per tenant and wallet_ref, outside the workspace), is put in one environment variable of the Acton process for a testnet call only, and is never in a request body, the argv, the run record or the result; exact occurrences in output are replaced before anything is stored. Testnet operations are declared only when a testnet RPC, a wallets file and an isolation command are configured. An attempt marker is created exclusively before Acton starts: if it cannot be written nothing is launched, and an existing marker means the attempt is not launched again. Dispatch answers NOT_SENT when the adapter or the connector's policy refuses before a process runs, when the binary cannot start, or when a read-only operation failed or was cut short; SENT when Acton ran; and INDEFINITE when a write or broadcast was cut short, exited non-zero, left no record or printed something other than its output contract (ERR_CONNECTOR_CONTRACT_DRIFT). Observe reads back the attempt's run record, and for a broadcast the transaction on testnet through the RPC; a marker with no record is UNKNOWN, never FAILED by absence. A result must satisfy the declared result schema.
config: HELM_GATEWAY_TON_ACTON_BIN and HELM_GATEWAY_TON_ACTON_WORKSPACE (absolute paths, both or neither) install the operations that do not run over tenant files.
HELM_GATEWAY_TON_ACTON_ISOLATION_CMD (a JSON array whose first element is an absolute program) adds the operations that run over tenant files.

HELM_GATEWAY_TON_TESTNET_RPC_URL and HELM_GATEWAY_TON_TESTNET_WALLETS_FILE (both or neither, only with the isolation command) add the testnet operations; HELM_GATEWAY_TON_TESTNET_MAX_SPEND is their per-action TON ceiling, default 1. These are operator-provided: the gateway chart does not mount a wallets file or set these variables yet.
protected_operations: Running Acton for a tenant, and broadcasting from the gateway's testnet wallet, through the Propose, Dispatch and Observe path of helm-gateway.
bypass_assumptions: Nothing confines Acton unless the operator's isolation command does. The gateway cannot see what the command does; the control claims only that the operations that run over tenant files are not declared without one, and that wallet secret files must be owner-only and outside the workspace. If the isolation command runs Acton under the gateway's own uid, or with a credential file mounted, tenant code can read it.
Mediation is observed-only for every operation: Acton runs on the gateway host and the workspace is reachable by whoever operates it, so the gateway is not the only path to any effect.

The testnet wallet secret is in the Acton process environment for the length of a testnet call. publish, topup and verify were not shown, against upstream Acton, to run no tenant-authored code; they are admitted on the strength of the isolation command and the .env and wallets.toml refusal, and the secret is a testnet key whose tenant owns the wallet_ref. A mainnet key must never be mounted. script.testnet, the one operation known to run tenant Tolk, is refused.
Redaction replaces exact occurrences of the secret only; an encoded or reversed copy in output is not recognised.

max_ton_spend is a declared ceiling compared with the configured ceiling; the amount actually spent is not measured against it. The testnet check shows a transaction with the printed hash exists on the account, not what it did.

A version or Tolk pin is confirmed only as a substring of acton --version output. A binary that does not print the Tolk compiler version makes every Tolk pin fail closed. The workspace file check is made before the run; a tenant can write a .env between the check and the run.

The broadcast output contract (one JSON object with address and tx_hash) and the variable ACTON_WALLET_SECRET are the gateway's declared interface to Acton, not qualified against a real Acton release; a release that differs makes testnet operations INDEFINITE, never SUCCEEDED.

The run record and the attempt marker are files in the tenant's workspace written by the gateway; anyone who can write there can forge or delete them. A forged record cannot confirm a broadcast, which also needs the RPC; a deleted marker and record read as FAILED by absence for an operation that left no other trace. Authority, reservations and receipts stay in Postgres.
Project paths inside a project are checked by pattern; Acton itself follows symlinks a project contains.

controls.title: Gateway sandbox effects stay in their tenant and hold no provider key
controls.claim: When an operator configures a sandbox provider, helm-gateway performs sandbox.create, sandbox.exec and sandbox.terminate through it (helm-tracker#266, P17): Docker, E2B, Daytona, OpenSandbox and Claude Managed Agents, behind one adapter. The provider and the sandbox come only from the effect's target (sandbox/{provider}[/{sandbox_id}], checked at Propose by effectargs.SandboxTarget and again by the adapter), never from its arguments, whose closed schemas admission checks and which carry no environment and no secret. The adapter compares the permit's argument digest with the bytes it acts on before any provider call. A sandbox it creates carries a label with a digest of the creating tenant and one with the attempt; exec and terminate act only on a sandbox that carries the calling tenant's label, and a sandbox of another tenant, or one the gateway did not create, is refused as one that does not exist (NOT_SENT, PRECONDITION_FAILED), so a provider account shared by tenants does not share its sandboxes. Create looks for a sandbox carrying its attempt's label before it writes and never creates a second; exec records its start, output and exit status in the sandbox and does not start twice for one attempt. The provider key is asked for from the gateway's custody (custody.SandboxKeys, the key file the operator mounted into the gateway Pod only) on every operation, handed to the provider client for that operation, and appears in no request body, URL, command, label, stored attempt, observation or receipt; a keyless provider (Docker) is never asked. A dispatch is NOT_SENT only when the effect certainly did not happen (a refusal before any write, or a provider 4xx other than 408; for exec, a wrapper status of 125 to 127 only when the sandbox's record, read back, shows no start, since a provider may derive that status from stderr the command wrote); a transport failure, a 5xx, a timeout, an answer too large or an answer of the wrong shape after a write is INDEFINITE (ERR_CONNECTOR_CONTRACT_DRIFT or PROVIDER_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE for the last two), and Observe reconciles it by reading the provider back: the sandbox inventory by label for create and terminate, and the record the command left in the sandbox for exec. A list answer that is not a list (null, {}, no items array) is ERR_CONNECTOR_CONTRACT_DRIFT, never an empty list, and a missing exec record is UNKNOWN, never FAILED: the command may have run and removed it. The command runs in a subshell, so a builtin (eval, exec, exit) cannot end the wrapper. An established result is a schema-checked artifact (admission.typedResult). Every provider answer is read through a size limit and no redirect is followed, so the key is never replayed to another host, and every provider URL must be an https URL (tls_required: false is refused), which stops the gateway at start, so no call, including the reads before a create, sends the key in clear. A create's limits and egress policy are applied by the provider or the create is refused (NOT_SENT): E2B and Daytona send none of them and refuse a create until they do. Claude Managed Agents commands run only on the customer's worker (a RemoteRunner over HTTPS with the custody's bearer token), never on the gateway's own host; its sandbox ids are random, every exec and terminate carries the tenant digest and the worker is to refuse another tenant's, an exec carries the egress policy and limits the worker is to apply, terminate calls the worker, and its egress changes are refused. Docker sandboxes are labelled containers from an image pinned by digest, with no environment, no mounts, no network, all capabilities dropped, a read-only root and `sleep` as the only entrypoint, so the image's own code never runs at create. With no provider configured the gateway has no sandbox effect type.
config: HELM_GATEWAY_SANDBOX_CONFIG_FILE: a JSON file (core/pkg/gateway/adapters/sandbox.Config) that lists the enabled providers and, for each provider that takes a key, the path of its key file (an operator mounts the Secret into the gateway Pod only; the Helm chart has no values for it yet). Unset, no sandbox effect type exists. A field that does not belong to a provider, an unknown field and a provider listed twice stop the gateway.

A tenant registers sandbox.create, sandbox.exec and sandbox.terminate as effect types with the risk classes the catalog declares (medium, high, low), and a mandate grants them over targets; the gateway's adapter does not grant.
protected_operations: Every sandbox.create, sandbox.exec and sandbox.terminate dispatch and read-back of helm.gateway.v1.EffectGatewayService and of the MCP tools on the worker and executor listeners, on helm-gateway serve.
The provider key for a sandbox effect: custody.SandboxKeys.Token, reached only through the adapter's TokenSource.
bypass_assumptions: The cloud providers' wire shapes (E2B, Daytona, OpenSandbox) follow each adapter's documented style and are proven only against fake provider servers; no provider account exists, so no live qualification has run. The Claude Managed Agents worker exec protocol v1 is defined by RemoteRunner and proven only against a fake worker; no worker in this tree implements it. Whether a worker binds a sandbox id to its first tenant, applies the egress policy and limits it is sent and ends a sandbox on terminate is the worker's promise: the gateway checks only that the worker echoes the tenant and says it applied the spec and terminated.

Tenant isolation is the label the adapter puts on a sandbox it creates. The provider account is shared: anyone who holds the account's key outside the gateway, or a provider feature that edits a sandbox's labels, can defeat it. The tenant label is a digest of the tenant id, not a secret.

sandbox.exec is declared high risk, but the effect type's risk class in a tenant's rows decides whether admission asks for approval and a step-up; a tenant that registers it lower runs commands without them.

Observe reads the command's result from the record the command's own sandbox keeps under /tmp/.helm/<attempt>. A command can overwrite or delete that record, so the result's trust class is sandbox_reported, never provider_readback, and a missing record leaves the exec UNKNOWN. The result carries the exit status, the output sizes and the first 8 KiB of each stream, not the complete output. A timed_out state means the command had not finished past its timeout and may still be running: neither the gateway nor the Docker provider kills it. The sandbox image needs sh, mkdir, date, cat, wc, mv and head; a sandbox that is gone before the read-back leaves the exec UNKNOWN.
A 4xx to a write is taken as a definite refusal (except 408). A provider that executes a write and then answers 4xx would make a NOT_SENT wrong.

A dispatch that looks for an existing sandbox and finds none, then creates, is not atomic with another gateway replica doing the same for the same attempt; the claim that consumes the permit is, and a permit is consumed once.

Claude Managed Agents sandboxes are session-scoped records in the gateway process (the adapter keeps them in memory). A restart zeroes only that record, not the worker: the sandboxes it held keep running on the worker and the gateway can no longer reach, read back or terminate them. Create makes bookkeeping directories under the configured workspace and outputs roots on the gateway host and makes no worker request; its create and terminate read-backs read the gateway's own record (trust class gateway_record, not provider_readback). The managed-agent receipts it computes are signed with the gateway's receipt key through Sign over the hash of the receipt body, not through SignReceipt over a gateway receipt, and are not stored in the gateway's ledger.

The Docker provider drives a docker CLI that talks to a daemon: access to a daemon socket is root-equivalent on that host. Use a private daemon (docker_socket), not the host's. The live Docker test skips without a daemon and a local image, so it is not one of this control's proofs.

The provider key is cached by the gateway's custody until its key file changes (custody providerKeyFile.reloadIfChanged), is handed to the provider client for each operation, and is not zeroed in the gateway process's memory.

The Docker provider's exec timeout stops the docker CLI, not the process in the container, and the gateway's wrapper does not kill a command past its timeout; a command that outlives its timeout keeps running until the sandbox ends.

A sandbox with network access is refused on Docker (the default bridge links the containers of different tenants and the host), and a disk limit is refused there; E2B and Daytona refuse every create until their create call carries the limits and the egress policy. The OpenSandbox create sends them, on a wire shape no live server has confirmed.

controls.title: The evaluated action and its effect class come from the request tuple and the catalog
controls.claim: Guardian selects the policy rule, and names an execution intent's allowed tool, from the typed request it signs (helm-tracker#304). One helper (boundActionID) serves the rule lookup and the intent, so they cannot name different tools. It reads params.tool_name only for the tool-call effect types (EXECUTE_TOOL, CALL_TOOL). On an evaluated request the context is the caller's, so bindRequestTool runs before any gate or the policy decision point reads it: for EXECUTE_TOOL it replaces the top-level tool_name of the context with the request resource, and for every other action it removes it, so the top-level tool_name that policy reads is never the caller's and a CALL_TOOL request is evaluated as CALL_TOOL. A tool_name nested in args or in another context member is left as the caller sent it. On the evaluate and ext-authz routes the request's effect class is a declaration: it is bound as effect_class with effect_class_source caller_declared, unless the kernel's effect type catalog knows the evaluated action, in which case the bound class is never below the catalog's (effect_class_source effect_catalog). The evaluated action is the request's action and, for EXECUTE_TOOL, its resource, which Guardian evaluates as the tool. The resource of any other action proves nothing about the action and does not change the class. A declaration that was not bound is kept as effect_class_declared. The organization-runtime route checks the activation ceiling against the bound class and attests the submitted one. ManagedPolicyPDP matches every rule against the request as bound without effect_class_source and effect_class_declared, the text a pattern written before those members existed was written for, so such a pattern matches as it did and no pattern reads either member at the top level. Deny and escalate rules are also matched against that reading with effect_class holding the declaration; allow rules never are, so an allow rule's effect_class selector and pattern read only the bound class. The MCP path marks its class tool_catalog and the governed proxy kernel_route. effect_class, effect_class_source and effect_class_declared are reserved: a top-level context member or MCP argument of one of these names from the caller is removed or refused (CTL-022) before the transport binds its own, and members of these names nested deeper are left as the caller sent them.
protected_operations: Policy rule selection and execution intent issuance for every Guardian decision.
The effect class bound for POST /api/v1/evaluate, the organization-runtime evaluate route, ext-authz and the governed OpenAI proxy.
bypass_assumptions: For an action the kernel's effect type catalog does not list (any tool name or URN, and CALL_TOOL), the class is the caller's declaration, whatever resource the request names. It is recorded as caller_declared and still selects class-keyed policy rules; a server-owned class for arbitrary tool names does not exist yet (helm-tracker#319).
On the evaluate route the tool itself is caller-declared: the kernel decides and signs for the tool the request names and does not dispatch it.
An in-process caller that builds an Effect of a tool-call type sets params.tool_name itself and is trusted to; only the evaluated-request path replaces or removes it.

Only ManagedPolicyPDP matches restricting rules against the kept declaration. A CEL or PRG expression that reads context.effect_class sees the bound class; one that restricted on a caller's label for a catalogued effect must read effect_class_declared.

A ManagedPolicyPDP pattern is an unanchored regular expression over the whole canonical request without the top-level effect_class_source and effect_class_declared, caller args and nested context included. Any pattern, including one that names tool_name, effect_class, effect_class_source or effect_class_declared, also matches a member of that name the caller nested in args or in another context member, which no transport removes. The effect_class, action and resource selectors read the bound values, and for deny and escalate rules also the kept declaration.

A ManagedPolicyPDP pattern never reads the top-level effect_class_source, so managed policy cannot restrict on who asserted the class: a deny pattern on caller_declared refuses only a request whose caller nested that member. A PRG expression on effect_class_source refuses caller-declared classes only where the PDP's ALLOW is not authoritative (no PDP, or the CEL/PRG runtime policy); under ManagedPolicyPDP an ALLOW replaces local PRG evaluation, so nothing refuses a caller-declared class until a typed effect_class_source selector exists (helm-tracker#322).

A pattern that relies on two context members being adjacent in the canonical text, or that matches a member name case-insensitively, depends on the caller's other members. A member the caller sends that sorts between the two (foo, or effect_class0, between effect_class and principal_id) ends the adjacency. Reserved names are removed only when the key, trimmed, is spelled exactly, and tool_name only when it is spelled exactly, so Effect_Class, EFFECT_CLASS or Tool_Name from the caller reaches policy and matches a (?i) pattern written for effect_class or tool_name.

The signed ext-authz response echoes the request's effect_class and risk_class as submitted and carries neither the bound class nor its source: when the kernel evaluated a higher class, a verifier of that response alone does not learn it. The evaluated class is in the decision's effect. Carrying it in the response is a contract change that has not been made.

The organization-runtime decision attestation carries the submitted effect class, because the control plane verifies that member against the effect_level it sent. The class the ceiling was checked against, its source and the declaration are in the decision record's input context, which the attestation does not sign. When the activation gate refuses the request, the decision record signed for the refusal carries no effect digest, so its signature does not cover that input context either.

The class binding covers the routes and paths named in protected_operations and MCP tool calls. The kernel bridge (core/pkg/bridge) evaluates EXECUTE_TOOL with no effect_class, and the MCP tool helm.verify evaluates the action and resource named in its arguments with no effect_class, so class-keyed rules, the P0 E4 denial included, do not match there.
The plan adapter (core/pkg/effectgraph) passes a step id as the request resource, so an EXECUTE_TOOL plan step selects the rule named by its step id; a CALL_TOOL step is evaluated as CALL_TOOL.

controls.title: Receipt verifiers match member names exactly and do not check unversioned receipts
controls.claim: A receipt verifier checks the receipt its reader reads, and checks a legacy receipt only when asked to (helm-tracker#305). receiptverify.ParseBundle and ParseReceipt, which receipt_verify, the WASM verifier, helm-ai-kernel verify receipt, POST /api/demo/verify and the receipt files of POST /api/v1/evidence/verify are parsed with, refuse a member that is a receipt, bundle, permit or gateway-binding member in another letter case, wherever a Go struct is decoded; those member names are read from the json tags of the Go types. The chain checks of the EvidencePack verifier (chain_integrity and lamport_monotonicity of helm-ai-kernel verify) decode a receipt file into contracts.Receipt only after receiptverify.ValidateReceiptMemberNames has applied the same member-name rules to it, and there a receipt.v5 receipt links only to a predecessor whose contracts.ReceiptChainHash, or the SHA-256 of whose file, is its prev_hash: a "hash" member a receipt declares about itself links only a successor with no signature_version. helm-ai-kernel evidence correlate-host applies ValidateReceiptMemberNames to each receipt file before it decodes one, and exits 2 naming a file it refuses. POST /api/demo/verify and POST /api/demo/tamper read their request body by exact member name and refuse any member but receipt, expected_receipt_hash and, for tamper, mutation, a letter-case variant of one of them included. Keys of maps and free-form values are compared exactly, and one name written twice is refused everywhere. In the bundle form a receipt member beside "receipts" is refused, so a reader cannot take a top-level verdict for a checked receipt's. A document nested deeper than 64 levels is refused before it is walked; the signature check of the EvidencePack verifier (embedded_signature_trust) fails for a file under receipts/ or 07_ATTESTATIONS/ that it refuses for that depth, and its reason counts such files as refused unread, not as signatures. A receipt with no signature_version is not checked. VerifyBundleWith answers with one error and no checks unless Options.AllowLegacyV4 is set, receipt_verify exits 2 without --allow-legacy-v4, and VerifyJSON, which the WASM verifier calls and which has no opt-in, reports UNVERIFIABLE. In core/pkg/crypto, ReceiptVerifyPayload, VerifyReceiptProfile and VerifyReceiptSignature return ErrLegacyReceiptRefused for a receipt with no signature_version unless given AllowLegacyReceiptPreimages, and no other option value opens the legacy preimage. Every VerifyReceipt method, KeyRing.VerifyReceipt included, takes no option and returns ErrLegacyReceiptRefused for such a receipt when it carries a signature. No shipped caller passes the option: the receipt signature check of POST /api/v1/evidence/verify reports an unversioned receipt as not checked (UNVERIFIABLE). The dev-local MCP branch of the EvidencePack verifier leaves an unversioned receipt unverified unless VerifyOptions.AllowLegacyV4Receipts is set, and embedded_signature_trust then says the receipt was not checked for want of a signature_version and names --allow-legacy-v4-receipts. Under every opt-in a legacy receipt whose receipt_id begins with "{" fails: it is a versioned signature replayed as a legacy receipt. An opted-in receiptverify result counts legacy_receipts, names every preimage in preimage_versions, and its identity check says a legacy signature does not cover verdict, tool_name or timestamp. The integrity check of receiptverify compares nothing and reports not_applicable, never a pass. key_id in a result is marked as the receipt's unsigned claim, and verify receipt lists the members its signature covers and the members it does not.
config: receipt_verify --allow-legacy-v4 (receiptverify.Options.AllowLegacyV4); helm-ai-kernel verify --allow-legacy-v4-receipts (verifier.VerifyOptions.AllowLegacyV4Receipts); and, for Go callers of core/pkg/crypto, AllowLegacyReceiptPreimages. None has an environment variable, and all default to refusing.
protected_operations: receipt_verify --receipt, receiptverify.VerifyJSON in the WASM verifier, helm-ai-kernel verify receipt, the receipt files and the receipt signature check of POST /api/v1/evidence/verify, the request bodies and receipts of POST /api/demo/verify and POST /api/demo/tamper, the dev-local MCP receipt check and the chain checks of helm-ai-kernel verify, and the receipt files helm-ai-kernel evidence correlate-host reads.
bypass_assumptions: Under an opt-in the replay of a versioned signature as a legacy receipt is refused by its receipt_id, which begins with "{". Everything a legacy signature never covered stays open under the opt-in: verdict, tool_name, timestamp and every member but the eight it signs can be rewritten on a receipt issued before receipt.v5, and the opted-in output says so.

Member names are matched exactly only where a Go struct is decoded from a document receiptverify has checked (ParseBundle, ParseReceipt, ValidateReceiptMemberNames). Keys of maps and free-form values (metadata, public_key_set, subject) are data: two keys there that differ in letter case are two keys. A member no decoded type names is ignored as before, except a receipt member at the top level of a bundle.

A bundle is refused for a receipt member beside receipts, in any letter case. A top-level member that is not a receipt member name (a comment, summary or paging member) is still ignored, so a reader must take a receipt's members from the entries of receipts and from nowhere else in the document.

The signature check of the EvidencePack verifier (embedded_signature_trust) reads receipt documents as maps, by exact member name, through receiptverify.ParseReceiptDocument: it refuses one name written twice, a member in another letter case is a separate member it does not read, and a file nested deeper than 64 levels is refused unread, fails the check and is counted in its reason as a file refused unread. Its chain checks (chain_integrity, lamport_monotonicity) decode each receipt file into contracts.Receipt after receiptverify.ValidateReceiptMemberNames has refused a member of a receipt, or of a struct a receipt holds, in another letter case, one name written twice at any depth, a trailing value, invalid JSON and nesting deeper than 64 levels; they do not apply the receipt.v5 member contract, because a pack holds receipts of more than one schema. In them a receipt.v5 successor links only to an identity recomputed from its predecessor, so a file put in a deleted receipt's place, signed or not, links it only if its contracts.ReceiptChainHash or the SHA-256 of its bytes is the successor's signed prev_hash. A successor whose signature_version is not receipt.v5 still links through a declared "hash", which has no specified preimage (security ledger F-20), so in a chain of such receipts a receipt can be replaced by a file that declares its hash. The chain checks do not see the last receipt of a chain deleted: the receipts left still link genesis-to-head. The signature check does not require every receipt file to be signed: an operator can strip the successor's signature members and hide a deletion with one fewer checked signature. A receipts/*.json file that is a bundle passes embedded_signature_trust unchecked and reads to the chain loader as a receipt with none of its members set; an array passes embedded_signature_trust the same way and fails the chain loader. Both predate this control and are left to helm-tracker#308. A Go consumer that decodes a pack's receipt file into contracts.Receipt parses it with receiptverify.ParseReceipt, or applies receiptverify.ValidateReceiptMemberNames first, as the chain checks and evidence correlate-host do.

POST /api/v1/evidence/verify and POST /api/demo/verify leave signature_profile and signature_algorithm to core/pkg/crypto (receiptverify.AnySignatureProfile), which verifies the hybrid and ML-DSA profiles. A signer of another type that exposes VerifyReceipt answers an unversioned receipt for itself.

A receipt.v5 signature covers 13 members. The other members of a single receipt, or of the last receipt of a chain, are covered by nothing; the integrity check and verify receipt say so and do not fail.
An unversioned DecisionRecord is a separate preimage with the same missing domain separation; it is outside this control.
